title: WPSS/1529/2015 of Smt Manju Tiwari AND ANOTHER Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 1529 of 2015
Smt. Manju Tiwari & another Ö Petitioners
Vs
State of Uttarakhand & others Ö Respondents
Mr. Amar Shukla, Advocate, present for the petitioners.
Mr. N.P. Sah, Standing Counsel, present for the State of Uttarakhand.
Ms. Prita Bhatt, Advocate holding brief of Ms. Beena Pande, Standing Counsel, present
for the State of U.P..
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)

1. The petitioners before this Court are the wife and
daughter respectively of a deceased employee, who was a
Constable in Uttar Pradesh Civil Police. After the creation of
the new State of Uttarakhand, he was transferred by the
authorities in Uttar Pradesh to Uttarakhand, which he failed to
join initially, but ultimately joined his service in Uttarakhand
on 12.08.2004 and thereafter he was dismissed from service by
the authorities in Uttarakhand on 03.01.2005. This order was
challenged by Mr. Swadesh Kumar Tiwari (who is the husband
of petitioner No. 1 ñ Smt. Manju Tiwari) before the Uttarakhand
State Public Service Tribunal, which was dismissed.
Subsequently, the appeal and the revison of the petitioner were
also dismissed. Thereafter, the petitioner filed a writ petition
before the Division Bench of this Court being WPSB No. 175 of
2011 which was allowed vide order dated 08.10.2013. It is
pertinent to mention here that meanwhile during the pendency
of the writ petition (WPSB No. 175 of 2011), the petitioner ñ
Swadesh Kumar Tiwari passed away and the present
petitioners have been impleaded as parties in the said petition.
The operative portion of the said judgment reads as under:-
ì2. The short question in the writ petition is,
whether SSP, Dehradun could be said to be the
Disciplinary Authority of the deceased petitioner. In the
absence of allocation of the deceased petitioner to the
State of Uttarakhand, SSP, Dehradun, who was an
authority of the State of Uttarakhand, had no
disciplinary jurisdiction over the deceased petitioner.
The fact remains that the transfer of the petitioner,
effected on 31st October, 2000, was cancelled on 20th

2
November, 2000. Deceased petitioner remained at
Kanpur.
3. We, accordingly, interfere, allow the writ
petition and, accordingly, set aside the judgment of the
Tribunal as well as the disciplinary order dated 3rd
January, 2005, appellate order dated 15th April, 2005
and the revisional order dated 1st August, 2005 only on
the ground that these orders were not passed by an
appropriate Disciplinary Authority, Appellate Authority
and Revisional Authority.î
2. From the perusal of the above judgment, it appears
that the reasoning adopted by the Division Bench of this Court
was that the husband of the petitioner ñ Manju Tiwari was
never an employee of Uttarakhand. Therefore, the authorities
in Uttarakhand had absolutely no jurisdiction to pass such an
order of dismissal. Subsequently, the present petitioners
moved a contempt petition being CLCON No. 183 of 2014
before this Court, which was dismissed as withdrawn by giving
certain liberties to the petitioners. The order dated 10.03.2015
passed in the contempt petition (referred above) reads as
under:-
 ìMr. Amar Shukla, Advocate for the applicants.
Mr. A.K. Joshi, Addl. C.S.C. for opposite party No. 1.
Mrs. Bina Pandey, Standing Counsel for the opposite
party No.2.
Learned counsel for the contempt applicants
submits that while quashing the termination order, no
direction has been issued to release the salary to the legal
heirs of the deceased petitioner / employee nor any
direction was issued to release the post retiral
benefits,therefore, applicants shall move appropriate
clarification / modification / review application before the
Division Bench.
In view of the above, learned counsel for the
applicants seeks permission to withdraw this contempt
application with the aforesaid liberty.
 Order accordingly.î
3. Consequently, the petitioners preferred
review/clarification application in WPSB No. 175 of 2011 for
clarification of the order dated 08.10.2013 (reference already
referred above), as the petitioners sought post retirement

3
benefit and other relief, therefore, the review application was
dismissed on the ground that this is absolutely fresh cause of
action. The Division Bench of this Court had dismissed the
review/clarification application of the petitioners vide order
dated 09.07.2015. The operative portion of the same reads as
under:-
ìA preliminary objection has been raised by learned
Standing counsel Mr. I.P. Kohli that in the main writ
petition, though the petitionerís wife and daughter were
substituted, at the relevant time, they have not made
such a prayer for post retiral dues, therefore, such prayer
cannot be granted in review petition. The contention of
the respondents seems to be correct.
In view thereof, the prayer for post retiral benefits at
this stage cannot be accepted, as it is a fresh cause of
action. Consequently, the review/clarification application
is totally misconceived. The review/clarification
application is hereby dismissed.
However, petitioners will be at liberty to file a fresh
writ petition for such relief. It is also made clear that
dismissal of the review/clarification application will not
prejudice to the case of the petitioners, in case, they file
fresh writ petition before appropriate court.î
4. Now the petitioners preferred present writ petition
before this Court. This Court on an earlier occasion clearly
indicated to the petitioners that relief they are seeking from
this Court is a separate cause of action, which can only be
given in a fresh writ petition but before an appropriate court.
5. Although counter affidavit has not been filed by the
State but it has raised preliminary objection that the writ
petition is not maintainable before this Court, as the husband
of the petitioner was never an employee of Government of
Uttarakhand, in fact, this is the reasoning given by the Division
Bench of this Court. It had already attained its finality and
relief has to be sought primarily from the Government of Uttar
Pradesh, as the petitioners resides in Itawa in Uttar Pradesh,
therefore, substantially the cause of action actually arises in
the State of Uttar Pradesh and not in Uttarakhand.

4
6. Merely because for a period of six months or so,
husband of the petitioner had worked in Uttarakhand will not
give him part cause of action here in Uttarakhand. Therefore,
the objection raised by the State appears to be correct.
7. In view of the above fact, it would not be proper to
entertain this writ petition, as the relief primarily has to be
given by the State of Uttar Pradesh, and no cause of action
arises in the State of Uttarakhand.
8. Accordingly, the writ petition is hereby dismissed.
However, the dismissal of the writ petition shall not prejudice
the case of the petitioner on merit.
(Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
05.11.2015
Aswal
